transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07 16:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rajesh Khanna (ApexAI CTO), Emily Rogers (ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (Infra)
Links referenced: <link:benchmark-sheet>, <link:security-pack>, <link:distro-samples>

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros then we can jump into the workload details. Rajesh, do you want to kick off with the ask?
[00:22] Rajesh (ApexAI): Yeah sure. Thanks Maya. We're trying to scope a POC to validate serving economics and latency for our new conversational agent. Main questions: what qps can we run on Dedicated vs Hosted, what's the p95 latency, and what's the cost delta when we enable batching and quant? Also need to check private deployment options for data residency.
[00:45] Maya: Great. High level we usually split the POC into three things: 1) traffic/traffic model, 2) benchmark runs to get baseline throughput/latency, 3) validation of security/networking. We'll need sample prompt distributions and a histogram for qps, concurrency, tokens in/out. Samir will walk through the benchmarking approach.
[01:05] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all. So for the traffic modelling part we want: steady-state qps, typical concurrent sessions, and peak bursts — how long those bursts last. Also token distribution: what's the median input tokens and the 95th percentile for outputs. That drives cache hit rates and KV cache sizing.
[01:30] Emily (ApexAI): For our alpha we see around 30 qps steady, spikes to ~250 for 15–45 minutes during peak events. Average user messages are short — 30–60 tokens in; generative replies are between 80 and 400 tokens, p95 around 600. But that's aggregated; we'll export exact histograms as requested.
[01:58] Carlos (Infra): On networking — we prefer VPC peering for the POC and want KMS integration for keys. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:18] Maya: Yes we do both KMS and HSM integrations on Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption but for Dedicated and Private we can do customer-managed KMS. We'll put the security pack in the notes.
[02:35] Rajesh: Two success criteria for the POC: hit p95 latency <= 200ms for typical queries at steady qps of 30, and demonstrate predictable cost per 1M tokens with <10% variance compared to forecast. If Dedicated can cut cost by 30% at our expected utilization we will move forward.
[02:58] Samir: Sounds reasonable. One nuance — p95 200ms depends heavily on token length and whether you use batching. If outputs are often 400–600 tokens, p95 will be higher. We need to model both "short" (<=150 tokens) and "long" (>=300 tokens) reply mixes.
[03:20] Maya: Let's talk numbers. Emily, can you share the split of short vs long generation? Even a rough percentage helps compute expected token throughput.
[03:32] Emily: Roughly 60% short, 35% long, 5% very-long. We'll send a sample CSV.
[03:45] Samir: Okay — for modeling: assume 30 qps steady * average output 180 tokens ~= 5.4k tokens/sec. With batching and KV caching enabled for prefixes we often see effective token cost drop by 20–40% depending on prompt reuse. For Dedicated, the unit-cost per token is lower but you need sustained utilization to amortize reserved capacity.
[04:15] Rajesh: What's your recommended minimal concurrency and instance type for Dedicated to hit our peak? Our peak is 250 qps for ~30 minutes.
[04:30] Samir: For that burst profile we'd design for a baseline of 50 concurrent model workers with autoscale to 200 for bursts. That maps to roughly N GPUs depending on model size/quant. If you're using a 70B quantized model, ballpark 4–6 A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline and autoscale to 20 for peaks — but we'll validate with a 48-hour run.
[05:00] Carlos: Can we run the baseline on your Dedicated infra in our VPC or will it use Redwood-managed infra? We need to ensure egress policies.
[05:12] Maya: For the POC we can run on Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (private deployment) or a dedicated project in our hosted fleet with strict tenancy. We'll capture traffic with telemetry and provide logs. We'll include the peering checklist in the security pack.
[05:38] Rajesh: Ok. On benchmarks — what inputs do you need from us exactly?
[05:50] Samir: Primary artifacts: 1) 7-day QPS histogram with 1-minute granularity, 2) list of 1000 anonymized sample prompts (representative), 3) desired success criteria e.g., p95 latency and cost expectations, 4) model candidate(s) you plan to use. With that we generate a traffic model and recommended footprint.
[06:18] Emily: We'll produce the histogram and 1k samples, but on models — we're exploring two families: an open 30B and an internal fine-tuned 13B. Cost/latency tradeoffs matter.
[06:32] Samir: That makes sense. 13B will have better latency and lower cost per token, but quality tradeoffs might exist. For the POC we usually run both back-to-back on the same traffic to compare.
[06:50] Rajesh: How do you measure cost per 1M tokens for these runs? Does it include infra + network + licensing?
[07:02] Maya: Our benchmark sheet will break down cost into compute (GPU hours), model licensing (if any), networking, and Redwood platform fees. We'll produce a token-level cost matrix. For Dedicated we show amortized cost at multiple utilization points (25/50/75% utilization).
[07:25] Carlos: Important — encryption at rest and audit logs. We need SOC 2 artifact and also ISO questionaire.
[07:38] Maya: We'll attach SOC 2 report and an ISO checklist, and we can provide live demo of audit log stream during the security call.
[07:52] Rajesh: Timeline — can you run the 48-hour baseline by Oct 20 if we send artifacts by Oct 10?
[08:02] Samir: Yes that timeline is plausible. We need the sample prompts and histograms by Oct 10, then we'll spin up the environments, run a dry-run, and schedule the 48-hour run the week of Oct 20.
[08:18] Emily: During the 48-hour run do you require us to expose real traffic? We prefer synthetic replay.
[08:26] Samir: Synthetic replay using your sample set is preferred. If you can provide original timestamps we can replay arrival patterns and preserve burst windows. We'll also do synthetic variations to stress batching and cache behavior.
[08:40] Rajesh: Great. A few technical clarifications: 1) How do you handle KV cache for multi-turn sessions? 2) How is fallback handled if a model variant is unavailable?
[08:52] Samir: 1) KV cache is per-session and can be pinned for a user stream to reduce recomputation for long contexts. We have eviction policies and metrics on cache hit ratio; you can tune TTL per route. 2) We support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and region-level routing. Fallback behavior and rollouts are part of the POC tests.
[09:10] Carlos: Any guidance on quantization profiles? Our infra team wants to pick between 4-bit and 8-bit quant for the POC.
[09:21] Samir: 4-bit quant loses a bit on quality but significant savings on memory and throughput. For 13B it's usually safe; for 30B you might prefer 8-bit or hybrid. We'll include recommended quant presets in the follow-up after we see samples.
[09:40] Maya: Let's document concrete success criteria for the POC so we can sign off. Proposed: 1) p95 <= 200ms at steady 30 qps for short/typical mix, 2) platform can support 250 qps bursts with p95 <= 500ms during the 30-minute window, 3) cost per 1M tokens on Dedicated at 50% utilization is at least 25% less than hosted baseline, 4) SOC2 + KMS requirements met. Agree?
[10:08] Rajesh: That matches our internal ask, yes.
[10:15] Emily: One more — we want to validate session affinity across autoscale, so long-running conversations don't lose context during scale events.
[10:25] Samir: We'll add a resilience test: scale up/down during active sessions and monitor state continuity and p99 errors.
[10:34] Maya: Good. Any blockers around data residency?
[10:40] Rajesh: We need EU-only data for some customers. Is Private deployment with regional control available for the POC?
[10:48] Maya: Yes, Private supports region-scoped control plane and data plane. For the POC we can pin the region to eu-west-1 and ensure logs and telemetry remain in-region; we'll note that in the security pack.
[11:05] Carlos: Networking specifics — we will provide VPC CIDRs and a list of allowed endpoints. We prefer a peered Dedicated option where control plane is customer-managed.
[11:16] Maya: We'll include the peering checklist and a recommended security group template in the pack.
[11:25] Rajesh: Ok. On the results dashboard — what telemetry will you provide post-run?
[11:33] Samir: We'll provide per-minute qps, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, batch sizes distribution, cache hit-rate, and cost breakdown per model/route. We'll share a preliminary dashboard and raw CSVs.
[11:50] Emily: Will you send the telemetry in a format we can ingest to our internal monitoring?
[11:56] Samir: Yes — CSV or JSON timeseries. We can also push to your S3 if you prefer.
[12:06] Rajesh: A quick note on competitor comparisons — we ran a small test on Bedrock and saw slightly higher p95 at similar cost. We want Redwood to show comparative numbers but not necessary to replicate their exact setup.
[12:22] Maya: We can include a comparative row in the benchmark sheet if you provide the reference data.
[12:30] Emily: Anything else we should clarify before the follow-up?
[12:34] Carlos: Backup plan for spikes that exceed the Dedicated capacity — is there automatic overflow to hosted?
[12:40] Samir: Yes, we can route overflow to a higher-cost hosted pool as a safety net. That will be part of the POC failover tests.
[12:50] Rajesh: Awesome. Let's recap and close with who does what.
[12:55] Maya: Recap: Redwood sends benchmark template + pricing sketch (Maya), SE runs modeling and profiles after receiving samples (Samir), Apex sends histograms and 1k sample prompts (Emily), infra provides VPC details (Carlos). Security review scheduled after artifacts.
[13:20] Rajesh: Sounds good. We'll aim to deliver by Oct 10.
[13:26] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the security call and the baseline run window. Anything else?
[13:35] Emily: One small ask — include a checklist of what we should sanitize when we send samples.
[13:40] Maya: We'll add a short data-sanitization checklist to the benchmark sheet.
[13:46] Rajesh: Thanks everyone, this was productive.
[13:50] Maya: Thanks — we'll circulate the artifacts and action items.

Transcript notes (qualities and artifacts):
- Auto-transcription had a few mis-heard acronyms ("V P C" transcribed a few ways).
- Speakers occasionally overlap; timestamps approximate.
- Technical terms: KV cache, prefix caching, quantization (4-bit/8-bit), autoscale, p95/p99, token throughput.

End of meeting.
